input.strategy_title: Surface model deployment status in the RHOAI Dashboard
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Data scientists deploying models through the Dashboard cannot tell whether a
deployment is healthy without leaving the console. InferenceService state is
only visible via `oc get inferenceservice` or by reading Kubernetes events,
which most Dashboard users cannot access. Support cases regularly begin with
"my model has been Pending for an hour" — information the platform already has
but does not surface.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Users see a deployment status (Ready, Progressing, Failed) for each deployed model in the Dashboard model serving views. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Users can open a status detail view showing the underlying condition messages and recent events for a failed or progressing deployment. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | Displayed status reflects the actual InferenceService state within 30 seconds of a change, without a manual page reload. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Users can filter and sort the deployed models list by status. |
| HLR-5 | P2 | Product documentation explains each status value and the first troubleshooting steps for Failed deployments. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- KServe

## Out of Scope

- Alerting or notifications on status transitions
- Status history / timeline views
- ModelMesh deployments (KServe InferenceService only)

## Open Questions

None blocking — KServe already exposes the needed conditions on the
InferenceService status; this strategy is about surfacing them.

# Surface InferenceService deployment status in Dashboard model serving views

## Description

This epic delivers deployment status visibility for KServe InferenceServices
inside the RHOAI Dashboard. Data scientists will see at a glance whether each
deployed model is Ready, Progressing, or Failed, can drill into the underlying
condition messages and recent events for failed or progressing deployments,
and see status stay current without a manual page reload. This removes the
need to leave the console and run `oc get inferenceservice` or read Kubernetes
events directly.

## Scope

- Add a deployment status (Ready, Progressing, Failed) for each deployed model
  in the Dashboard model serving views, derived from the InferenceService CR
  status conditions (e.g. Ready, PredictorReady) and related Kubernetes events.
- Add a status detail view for a deployment showing the underlying condition
  messages and recent events, reachable for failed or progressing deployments.
- Keep the displayed status within 30 seconds of the actual InferenceService
  state without requiring a manual page reload (refresh mechanism — e.g.
  polling or watch — is an implementation decision for the Dashboard team).
- Filter and sort by status (HLR-4) is not part of this epic: it is a
  distinct, deferrable capability delivered by a separate P2 epic owned by the
  same team, so it can be planned and deferred independently of this P0 work.
- KServe itself requires no code changes: the conditions and events are
  already exposed on the InferenceService status. The serving team's
  validation of that status-condition contract runs in parallel with this
  work and owns the authoritative recommended condition-to-display-state
  mapping; this epic consumes that recommendation as a non-blocking input and
  coordinates any rendering deviations with the serving team.
- Out of scope per strategy: alerting/notifications on status transitions,
  status history / timeline views, and ModelMesh deployments (KServe
  InferenceService only).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a deployed KServe InferenceService, when a user opens the Dashboard
  model serving views, then each deployed model shows a status of Ready,
  Progressing, or Failed (HLR-1).
- Given a failed or progressing deployment, when the user opens its status
  detail view, then the underlying condition messages and recent events for
  that deployment are shown (HLR-2).
- Given a change in the actual InferenceService state, the displayed status
  reflects it within 30 seconds, without a manual page reload (HLR-3).
- The Ready/Progressing/Failed mapping is derived from the InferenceService
  status conditions as documented in the KServe architecture context
  (serving.kserve.io/v1beta1 conditions such as Ready and PredictorReady).
- ModelMesh deployments are not covered by the status display (strategy
  out-of-scope).
- The Dashboard's existing build pipeline remains green with these changes.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): status shown per deployed model — this epic.
- HLR-2 (P0): status detail view with conditions and events — this epic.
- HLR-3 (P1): 30-second freshness without manual reload — this epic.
- HLR-4 (P2): filter and sort by status — separate P2 epic owned by the same
  team (distinct, deferrable capability; split so it can be planned and
  deferred independently of this P0 work).

# Validate KServe InferenceService status-condition contract for Dashboard consumption

## Description

This epic delivers a validation of the existing KServe InferenceService
status-condition and event contract that the Dashboard's deployment-status
surfacing relies on. KServe requires no code changes — the serving team
confirms that the conditions and events already exposed by the platform are
complete, stable, and correctly interpretable for rendering Ready /
Progressing / Failed states, and hands any gaps to the Dashboard effort.
The strategy marks this as non-blocking, so this validation runs in parallel
with the Dashboard implementation.

## Scope

- Confirm the set of InferenceService status conditions (e.g. Ready,
  PredictorReady) exposed via serving.kserve.io/v1beta1, and their semantics,
  in both serverless and raw deployment modes.
- Confirm that the conditions are sufficient to distinguish the Ready,
  Progressing, and Failed display states the Dashboard must render, and
  document the recommended condition-to-display-state mapping. This epic owns
  the authoritative mapping: the Dashboard status-surfacing effort consumes
  it as a non-blocking input rather than deriving a competing mapping.
- Confirm that relevant Kubernetes events (e.g. predictor failures, route
  issues) are observable for failed and progressing InferenceServices and
  carry useful messages for the status detail view.
- Document findings — including any condition or event coverage gaps that
  would prevent accurate status display — and hand them to the Dashboard
  effort. Gaps are escalated as recommendations, not silently patched: no
  KServe code changes are in scope for this epic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The InferenceService status conditions relevant to deployment health are
  inventoried, with their semantics, across serverless and raw deployment
  modes.
- A documented mapping from condition states to the Ready / Progressing /
  Failed display states is produced and handed off.
- For a failing and for a progressing InferenceService, the observable
  Kubernetes events are confirmed to include recent, informative messages
  suitable for the status detail view.
- Any gaps that would prevent accurate status display are documented with
  remediation recommendations and communicated to the Dashboard team.
- No KServe code changes are required as part of this validation (per the
  strategy: KServe already exposes the needed conditions).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): status shown per deployed model — validates the data-source
  contract behind this requirement (parallel, non-gating per strategy).
- HLR-2 (P0): status detail view conditions and events — confirms the
  condition messages and events the detail view will surface.

# Document deployment status values and Failed-deployment troubleshooting

## Description

This epic delivers product documentation for the Dashboard's new deployment
status feature: an explanation of each status value (Ready, Progressing,
Failed) shown in the model serving views, and the first troubleshooting steps
a user should take for a Failed deployment. This is substantive new
documentation content, authored through the Red Hat docs content process
after the implementation work has landed so the docs describe what was
actually built.

## Scope

- A documentation topic explaining each deployment status value (Ready,
  Progressing, Failed) displayed for deployed models in the Dashboard model
  serving views.
- First troubleshooting steps for Failed deployments, oriented around the
  status detail view's condition messages and recent events (e.g. how to open
  the detail view and what the common condition messages mean).
- Content authored in the Documentation component's docs repository following
  the Red Hat docs content process.
- Out of scope per strategy: alerting/notifications, status history, and
  ModelMesh deployments — the documentation covers KServe
  InferenceService-based deployments only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation explains each status value (Ready, Progressing, Failed) shown
  in the Dashboard model serving views (HLR-5).
- Documentation includes the first troubleshooting steps for Failed
  deployments, referencing the status detail view and its condition messages
  and events (HLR-5).
- Content is technically reviewed against the implemented behavior of the
  deployment-status feature and the validated KServe condition semantics
  before publication.
- Content follows the Red Hat docs content process for the Documentation
  component.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-5 (P2): product documentation for status values and Failed-deployment
  troubleshooting — this epic.

# Filter and sort the deployed models list by deployment status

## Description

This epic adds filter and sort controls to the deployed models list in the
RHOAI Dashboard model serving views, keyed on the deployment status (Ready,
Progressing, Failed). It is a distinct, deferrable enhancement: users get
full status visibility from the status-surfacing work without it, and this
epic can be planned, scheduled, or deferred independently because it is a
separate P2 requirement in the strategy.

## Scope

- Add a status filter to the deployed models list so users can narrow the
  list to deployments in a selected status (Ready, Progressing, Failed).
- Add status-based sorting to the deployed models list.
- Build on the existing deployed-models list UI and the deployment status
  values rendered by the Dashboard's status-surfacing work; no new data
  sources, no backend changes, and no KServe changes — the underlying
  InferenceService conditions already exist in-platform.
- Runs alongside the status-surfacing work in the same repo and team; the
  shared list surface is a merge-coordination concern managed within the
  team, not a blocking dependency.
- Out of scope per strategy: alerting/notifications on status transitions,
  status history / timeline views, and ModelMesh deployments (KServe
  InferenceService only).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the deployed models list, when the user applies a status filter, then
  only deployments with the selected status (Ready, Progressing, or Failed)
  are shown (HLR-4).
- Given the deployed models list, when the user sorts the list by status,
  then deployments are ordered by status according to the selected sort
  direction (HLR-4).
- The deployed models list remains fully usable when no filter is applied
  (no regression to the unfiltered list).
- The Dashboard's existing build pipeline remains green with these changes.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): filter and sort the deployed models list by status — this epic
  (split from the P0 status-surfacing work so the P2 capability can be
  planned and deferred independently).

below-threshold escape conditions do not apply.

| KServe | Passive (no code changes; conditions and events already exposed) | RHOAI Serving | Strategy relies on KServe's existing InferenceService status contract. Because the passive component is owned by a different team than the active component, a separate validation Implementation epic (E002) owned by RHOAI Serving confirms the contract; this is not folded into the Dashboard epic's ACs. |
| Documentation | Docs target for HLR-5 (substantive new content) | RHOAI Documentation (assumed — see Health Warnings) | docs-authoring Implementation epic E003 |

None. The strategy's only open-questions entry states "None blocking — KServe
already exposes the needed conditions on the InferenceService status", and no

mapping) are implementation details for the Dashboard team, captured as
acceptance criteria, not genuine unknowns.

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Component | Priority |
|----|-------|------|------|-----------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9001-E001 | Surface InferenceService deployment status in Dashboard model serving views | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | Dashboard | P0 |

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001["E001 Dashboard status surfacing (P0)"] --> E003["E003 Status documentation (P1)"]
    E002["E002 KServe condition contract validation (P1)"] --> E003
    E004["E004 Filter/sort models list by status (P2)"] --> E003
```

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| (root) E001 | — | Dashboard implementation is unblocked: the InferenceService status conditions and events it consumes already exist in-platform (architecture context, kserve.md); the strategy marks nothing blocking. |
| (root) E002 | Rule 14 | Validation of an existing contract in a different repo (kserve) with no artifact produced that E001 builds against — the conditions already exist; E002 confirms them. Parallel by design; a serial edge would mis-sequence independent work. |
| (root) E004 | Rule 15 | Same repo and team as E001, different area of the same list surface (filter/sort controls vs. status surfacing). E004 consumes status values already derived from in-platform InferenceService conditions — no artifact produced by another epic that E004 builds against — so the shared list surface is merge-coordination risk within one team, not a blocking dependency. Also kept parallel so the P2 feature can be deferred without touching the P0 path. |
| E001 → E003 | Rule 11 | docs-authoring is blocked by all Implementation epics — docs describe what was built. |
| E002 → E003 | Rule 11 | Same: documentation of status values must reflect the validated condition semantics, not just the Dashboard rendering. |

## Criterion Details

### 1. HLR Coverage (2/2)
All five HLRs map to at least one epic: HLR-1/HLR-2 (P0) → E001 (with E002
validating the data-source contract), HLR-3 (P1) → E001, HLR-4 (P2) → E004,

the per-epic HLR Traceability sections. Priority inheritance is correct: E001
is P0 (highest of HLR-1..3); the P2 filter/sort capability was split into E004
rather than collapsed into the P0 epic — this is the correct application of
the priority-split rule (distinct, deferrable user capability with independent
value). E003 (docs-authoring) correctly derives P1 from the strategy's
`priority: Major` via the docs-authoring exception, not from inheritance, and
its Rule 11 edges are correctly not treated as priority-inheriting. E002 is
P1 while tracing to P0 HLRs — defensible, because it blocks no downstream
work (the strategy explicitly marks the validation non-blocking) and the
choice is flagged in Health Warnings for verification; noted as a minor
observation, not an inheritance error.

### 2. DAG Coherence (2/2)
No circular dependencies; no invalid edges. The diagram (`graph TD`,
dependency → dependent) matches epic frontmatter `dependencies` exactly in
both directions: E001/E002/E004 are roots with empty `dependencies`, and E003
lists all three. Edge justification checks out: E002 as a root is correct
under Rule 14 (different repo, no build-against artifact — the conditions
already exist in-platform); E004 as a root is correct under Rule 15 (same
repo/team, different area of the list surface — merge coordination, not
dependency), which also preserves independent deferrability of the P2 work.
Rule 11 is satisfied: the docs-authoring epic (E003) is blocked by all three
Implementation epics. No konflux-onboarding epics exist, so Rules 7/8/10
parallelism constraints do not apply; no conditional branch files exist.
Critical path length 2 fits the S-size heuristic (1-2). Cross-check of epic
content found no uncaptured data/artifact dependency: E001's consumption of
E002's condition-to-display-state mapping is a design recommendation handled
as a non-blocking coordinated input (per the strategy's explicit "None
blocking" statement), and E001's own AC grounds the mapping in the KServe
architecture context, so no build-against artifact edge is required. Minor
observation: E002's scope calls its mapping "authoritative" while E001's AC
derives the mapping from architecture context — the hand-off language could
be tighter, but the parallel-edges decision is correct.

### 3. Epic Boundaries (2/2)
Each epic has a clean component/team tuple: E001/E004 (Dashboard / RHOAI
Dashboard), E002 (KServe / RHOAI Serving), E003 (Documentation / RHOAI
Documentation). E002 correctly applies the passive-component exception (KServe
needs no code changes, but a different team validates it → separate validation
Implementation epic rather than folding into the Dashboard epic's ACs). The
E001/E004 split is along the sanctioned priority/deferrability axis, not a
duplicate-surface split: E004 builds filter/sort controls on top of the status
values E001 renders and does not independently rebuild any data structure or
UI surface. No work-product type mixing — code implementation (E001/E002/E004)
and content authoring (E003) are in separate epics. No epic approaches
multi-sprint size.

### 4. Type Correctness (2/2)
All epics are typed Implementation and all produce concrete artifacts (UI
features; a validation report plus condition-to-display-state mapping; doc
topics; filter/sort controls). E002 is the correct classification under Rule
4: its outcome does not change which downstream epics exist or what they do
(gaps are escalated as recommendations, no KServe changes), so it is properly
an Implementation producing a deliverable rather than an Investigation — and
the summary explicitly records this reasoning. No `gated_by`/`gate_failure_impact`
fields are set anywhere, which is consistent with there being no Investigation
epics and no true gates. `implementation_type: docs-authoring` on E003 is
correct.

### 5. AI Implementability Scoring (2/2)
All four epics are Implementation type and all carry the 9-signal `ai_signals`
set (none misuse `investigation_signals`); rationale files exist for all four.
Signal values were checked against the rubric, the strategy, and the
architecture context: E001/E004's `pattern_precedent: 1` and
`architecture_claims: 1` are corroborated by the Dashboard architecture
context (resource lists/status views as the standard surface); E002's

defined deliverable; E003's `human_process_gates: -1` (docs technical
review), `repo_access: 0` (docs repo unidentified — no architecture context
file for Documentation), and `existing_foundation: 0` (unverifiable) are all
correctly scored unfavorable/neutral with matching rationales. `open_questions:
1` across the code epics is consistent with the strategy's "None blocking"
statement. No signal contradictions found; computed totals/scores were not
re-derived per instructions.

### 6. Acceptance Criteria Quality (2/2)
Every epic has testable, HLR-derived acceptance criteria. Rule-mandated ACs
are present where applicable: E003 (docs-authoring) carries the Rule 24
"technically reviewed against the implemented behavior... before publication"
AC. No epic has a konflux-onboarding dependency chain (Dashboard and KServe
are already onboarded; Documentation goes through the docs content process),
so Rule 25 does not strictly apply — E001 and E004 nonetheless include
build-pipeline-green ACs, which is harmless. This is a new capability, not a
replacement, so no rollback/feature-flag AC is required. No epic body
references sibling epics by bare draft ID (cross-epic references use team/
capability descriptions), so no draft-ID citations to flag.

### 7. Completeness (2/2)
The combined epic set accounts for the full strategy scope: status surfacing,
detail view with conditions and events, 30-second freshness without manual
reload, filter/sort, and product documentation. Strategy out-of-scope items
(alerting/notifications, status history/timeline, ModelMesh) are carried into
the epic scopes rather than silently dropped or violated. The strategy's
open-questions context ("KServe already exposes the needed conditions") is
carried forward and drives both the no-Investigation decision and E002's

so the cross-epic flow is accounted for. No conditional branches are needed
(no bounded unknowns). Documentation support is required via HLR-5 and the
docs-authoring epic E003 exists, with its owner-team assumption transparently
flagged in Health Warnings (a strategy gap — no Impacted Teams table — not a
decomposition defect).
